title: The Errand
summary: Carrie arrives with one DTI errand while the household is already eating breakfast; Gunnar treats the appointment as a route to learn, not a mystery to worship.

panelPlan.action: Morning in the Safe Cave. Astrid and the two male Kin remain together around breakfast and simple household tasks while Carrie puts an appointment slip and two MetroCards on the table.
Gunnar reads the numbered address and transit line without touching the cards.
Bjorn finishes coffee.
The three Kin continue breakfast rather than preparing to follow.
Gunnar pockets one MetroCard.

dialogueInline.text: One errand. That is the whole day.
A housing confirmation stamp. No oaths. No blood. Ideally no property damage.
Then I should know the road.

title: The Key Stays Home
summary: Before leaving, Bjorn gives Astrid the apartment key, a small sign that the household already exists independently of the two men Carrie usually takes into the city.
settingText: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hall

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hall
panelPlan.action: Bjorn reaches for the brass key, then looks back at Astrid and the two male Kin staying in 5B.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hall
panelPlan.action: He places the key in Astrid's palm.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hall
panelPlan.action: Astrid closes her hand around it without ceremony.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hall
panelPlan.action: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar step into the hall while the three Kin remain together inside.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hall
panelPlan.action: Carrie notices the handoff but does not comment.

title: Burial Road
summary: The subway entrance is still intimidating, but Gunnar responds by watching people use it rather than turning the threshold into a refusal.

panelPlan.action: The trio stops above the subway stairs as commuters move around them.
Bjorn looks down into the station.
Gunnar watches three unrelated commuters descend without hesitation.
A commuter brushes past with a coffee and disappears underground.
Gunnar starts down.

dialogueInline.text: You did not say burial road.

title: The Gate Refuses Her
summary: Carrie's demonstration fails, making room for Gunnar to learn by watching rather than for the issue to spend pages explaining transit technology.

panelPlan.action: Carrie takes one MetroCard and demonstrates a confident swipe.
The turnstile flashes rejection.
An impatient commuter gestures without stopping.
Bjorn looks at Carrie.
Carrie flips the card and tries again.

dialogueInline.text: The iron is old and badly maintained.

title: Gunnar Reads the Swipe
summary: Gunnar solves the turnstile by observing commuter rhythm and body mechanics, establishing his adaptation as practical pattern reading rather than magic-system decoding.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar steps aside and silently watches several commuters swipe and push through.
His attention follows card angle, hand speed and the timing of pressure against the bar.
He swipes once and passes cleanly.
Carrie stares.
Bjorn takes the card from Gunnar.

title: The Iron Worm Arrives
summary: The first train arrival is allowed to be frightening and physical, then immediately ordinary because New Yorkers simply board it.

panelPlan.action: A train roars into the station; Bjorn braces instinctively while Gunnar tracks the braking lights and door positions.
The train stops exactly where commuters expected.
Doors open and people exit around Bjorn without acknowledging his stance.
Gunnar steps aboard first, eyes on the route strip above the doors.
Bjorn follows.

dialogueInline.text: The iron worm screams before battle.
It has swallowed worse things than us.

title: Crowd Without Banners
summary: Inside the train, Bjorn begins learning that dense public space has rules nobody announces, while Gunnar watches how riders create room for one another without command.

panelPlan.action: Packed train car. Bjorn occupies too much doorway space until the crowd naturally routes around him.
Carrie gently pulls him one step away from the doors.
Gunnar watches a rider fold inward to let a stroller pass.
Bjorn copies the movement when another passenger needs the pole.
The train leaves the station with all three embedded in ordinary commuter life.

dialogueInline.text: In New York, that is just getting on.

title: The Busker
summary: A busker turns the trip into the first moment of warmth with a stranger, giving Bjorn a social encounter that is not about failing a system.

panelPlan.action: A busker finishes a song in the car or on the platform and passes a small container for tips.
Bjorn listens with unexpected seriousness.
Carrie drops a dollar in the container.
Bjorn nods solemnly to the busker.
Gunnar smiles at Bjorn rather than at the modern object.

title: Between Stations
summary: Carrie's work problem changes the route while Gunnar is already learning station order, showing that useful navigation grows inside an ordinary conversation rather than from a puzzle page.

panelPlan.action: Carrie's phone buzzes. She answers while Gunnar follows station names above the door.
DTI supervisor voice through phone.
Carrie closes her eyes.
Gunnar points to the next transfer stop on the route strip.
Carrie checks her phone map, then looks at him.

dialogueInline.text: The annex function moved. Your appointment is at the temporary office.
The function moved. Of course it did.

title: Above Ground
summary: The trio emerges into an unfamiliar part of the city and Gunnar orients from physical cues while Carrie is still fighting the updated address on her phone.
settingText: Midtown or downtown street near the temporary DTI annex

panelPlan.location: Midtown or downtown street near the temporary DTI annex
panelPlan.action: They come up a different subway exit into a dense avenue with trucks, scaffolding and cross traffic.

panelPlan.location: Midtown or downtown street near the temporary DTI annex
panelPlan.action: Carrie rotates her phone trying to match the moved annex address.

panelPlan.location: Midtown or downtown street near the temporary DTI annex
panelPlan.action: Gunnar looks at the sun angle, numbered cross street and flow of traffic rather than her screen.

panelPlan.location: Midtown or downtown street near the temporary DTI annex
panelPlan.action: He points one block over.

panelPlan.location: Midtown or downtown street near the temporary DTI annex
panelPlan.action: Bjorn starts walking with Gunnar.

dialogueInline.text: This says we are facing west. We are not facing west.
I trust that my phone currently does not.

title: Lunch Window
summary: A short food stop lets Bjorn and Gunnar experience the city between destinations, and Carrie's repeated small expenditures quietly continue Bjorn's discomfort with dependence.
settingText: Street food cart / sidewalk near DTI annex

panelPlan.location: Street food cart / sidewalk near DTI annex
panelPlan.action: Carrie stops at a hotdog cart because the appointment was pushed and nobody has eaten since morning.

panelPlan.location: Street food cart / sidewalk near DTI annex
panelPlan.action: The vendor hands over three hotdogs while Bjorn watches Carrie pay.

panelPlan.location: Street food cart / sidewalk near DTI annex
panelPlan.action: Gunnar studies the cart's small ecosystem: vendor, regular customer, delivery bike, condiment bottles.

panelPlan.location: Street food cart / sidewalk near DTI annex
panelPlan.action: Bjorn takes one bite and decides the food is acceptable.

panelPlan.location: Street food cart / sidewalk near DTI annex
panelPlan.action: The vendor has already moved on to the next customer.

dialogueInline.text: You can hate me after you eat.

title: Nothing Useful
summary: Gunnar spends a few minutes watching city life without mapping it, the first explicit hint that his attention may become personal curiosity rather than permanent navigation duty.
settingText: Small public seating area near the annex

panelPlan.location: Small public seating area near the annex
panelPlan.action: The trio sits on a low wall or small public bench finishing lunch while pedestrians cross the frame.

panelPlan.location: Small public seating area near the annex
panelPlan.action: Gunnar watches a dog refuse to move, a cyclist lock up, and office workers argue over coffee.

panelPlan.location: Small public seating area near the annex
panelPlan.action: Bjorn notices Gunnar has no map, paper or transit card in his hands.

panelPlan.location: Small public seating area near the annex
panelPlan.action: Gunnar keeps watching the street.

panelPlan.location: Small public seating area near the annex
panelPlan.action: Carrie hears the answer and, for once, does not give them another instruction.

title: The House Hides Its Name
summary: The destination finally appears, undercutting the idea that successful navigation means institutions themselves are legible.

panelPlan.action: Plain temporary municipal office exterior with a small DTI paper sign taped behind glass and older building signage still visible.
Bjorn compares the appointment slip with the nearly hidden sign.
Carrie checks the number twice.
Gunnar notices several employees entering around the side.

dialogueInline.text: This house hides its true name.
This house lost a budget meeting.

title: The Closed Side Entrance
summary: Contradictory posted directions become one concise obstacle instead of the whole issue, and Gunnar again reads what people actually do.
settingText: Temporary DTI annex exterior / side door

panelPlan.location: Temporary DTI annex exterior / side door
panelPlan.action: A front-door notice points to SIDE ENTRANCE; the side entrance has a paper notice pointing back toward reception.

panelPlan.location: Temporary DTI annex exterior / side door
panelPlan.action: Carrie reads both signs.

panelPlan.location: Temporary DTI annex exterior / side door
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks between them.

panelPlan.location: Temporary DTI annex exterior / side door
panelPlan.action: Gunnar watches an employee carrying coffee use an unmarked service door.

panelPlan.location: Temporary DTI annex exterior / side door
panelPlan.action: Carrie follows his gaze.

title: The Hidden Hall
summary: Carrie reluctantly follows the route staff actually use, while Bjorn recognizes the invisible labor infrastructure underneath an institution that looks confusing from the front.
settingText: DTI annex service entrance and interior corridor

panelPlan.location: DTI annex service entrance and interior corridor
panelPlan.action: The three enter through the working service door alongside a maintenance worker with a cart.

panelPlan.location: DTI annex service entrance and interior corridor
panelPlan.action: Gunnar holds the door for the worker rather than blocking it.

panelPlan.location: DTI annex service entrance and interior corridor
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks at supply carts, taped arrows and employee doors.

panelPlan.location: DTI annex service entrance and interior corridor
panelPlan.action: Carrie points down a corridor marked RECEPTION.

panelPlan.location: DTI annex service entrance and interior corridor
panelPlan.action: They move with staff flow rather than wandering deeper.

dialogueInline.text: We are not calling this breaking in.
Hidden roads for those who keep the hall alive.
Hallway. We are calling it a hallway.

title: Reception
summary: The remaining bureaucratic comedy is compressed into one reception beat: the original-copy contradiction, chained pen, and required sign-in all happen at the same desk.

panelPlan.action: Plain reception desk with paper sign-in sheet, chained blue pen and stacks of moved-office folders.
Bjorn looks at the chained pen.
Carrie presents the housing confirmation.
Receptionist inspects it.
Gunnar watches the stamp pad beside the clerk.

dialogueInline.text: You trust the oath but not the pen.
Then she meant the copy marked original.

title: The Stamp
summary: The actual errand ends quickly once they reach the right desk, deliberately refusing to let the institution occupy the final third of the issue.

panelPlan.action: The receptionist stamps the housing confirmation.
Carrie looks at the now-completed page.
Gunnar waits for the next instruction.
Bjorn looks toward the exit.
They leave the desk while another ordinary case is already moving into their place.

dialogueInline.text: That was the entire stupid errand.
Then we have won very little.

title: Do We Have to Go Home?
summary: With the required task complete, Gunnar asks whether travel can include a choice that serves no administrative purpose.

panelPlan.action: Outside, Carrie folds the stamped confirmation into her folder and starts toward the subway.
Gunnar stays where he is for one beat.
Carrie looks at him, unsure what problem he has found.
Gunnar points toward a side street he noticed earlier.
Bjorn studies him, then starts in that direction.

dialogueInline.text: Do we have to go directly?
I want to see what is there.

title: One Block Wrong on Purpose
summary: Gunnar deliberately takes a route that is unnecessary, converting navigation from survival skill into personal curiosity.
settingText: Ordinary city side street and small public plaza

panelPlan.location: Ordinary city side street and small public plaza
panelPlan.action: The trio walks one block off the efficient route into a small plaza with trees, food workers on break, parents, bikes and a public sculpture.

panelPlan.location: Ordinary city side street and small public plaza
panelPlan.action: Gunnar slows to look at the sculpture and the people using the square around it.

panelPlan.location: Ordinary city side street and small public plaza
panelPlan.action: Carrie checks the time and almost speaks, then puts her phone away.

panelPlan.location: Ordinary city side street and small public plaza
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks back toward the subway entrance they passed.

panelPlan.location: Ordinary city side street and small public plaza
panelPlan.action: Gunnar smiles slightly.

dialogueInline.text: This is not the road home.
That is why I chose it.

title: Five Minutes
summary: Carrie allows the day to contain five purposeless minutes, and the three begin to feel less like caseworker plus assignment and more like people sharing time.

panelPlan.action: They sit on a public bench. Gunnar watches the square; Bjorn people-watches; Carrie has the folder closed beside her.
A work notification lights Carrie's phone. She silences it without opening the message.
Bjorn notices.
Gunnar watches a child chase a pigeon across the square and says nothing.
For one panel nobody is solving anything.

title: Get Us Home
summary: Carrie hands Gunnar the return journey, turning his accumulated observation into responsibility rather than a trick he performs for approval.

panelPlan.action: They stand at the subway entrance after the break.
Carrie holds out the two MetroCards toward Gunnar.
Gunnar takes them without looking surprised.
Bjorn steps toward the stairs.
Gunnar goes first.

dialogueInline.text: That is usually what home means.

title: The Transfer
summary: A real service change tests Gunnar once, and he solves it from physical traces and commuter behavior rather than requiring several pages of transit exposition.

panelPlan.action: At a transfer junction, a temporary service notice redirects one line while an older arrow remains visible underneath.
Carrie starts to open her phone.
Gunnar studies the exposed older arrow, yellow tape and the direction most commuters are taking.
He points down a corridor.
Carrie checks the sign, then follows.

dialogueInline.text: The city changed its mind but left scars.

title: Different Stair
summary: Gunnar chooses a different station exit from the one they used that morning and proves he is navigating the neighborhood rather than memorizing a single route.

panelPlan.action: They emerge from a different Bushwick staircase into late-afternoon neighborhood light.
Gunnar points down the block toward familiar storefronts.
Carrie recognizes the bodega awning in the distance.
Gunnar looks pleased without performing triumph.

dialogueInline.text: This is not the stair we entered.
It is the stair we need.
Okay. I know where we are.

title: The Block Again
summary: Returning through the familiar block lets the day's new competence re-enter ordinary neighborhood life instead of ending at the transit system itself.

panelPlan.action: The trio walks past the bodega and apartment block; the same street that felt like strange territory now reads as recognizable geography.
Bjorn looks toward the bodega.
Carrie keeps walking.
Gunnar checks no map and keeps pace.

dialogueInline.text: We still owe the downstairs man proper money.

title: Home Opens
summary: The return is completed by the people waiting inside: Astrid opens the door with the key Bjorn left her, making home a relationship rather than merely a destination.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn knocks once at 5B. Astrid opens the door with the brass key still in hand; the two male Kin are visible behind her in the functioning apartment.
Astrid looks at the three travelers.
Bjorn steps inside.
Gunnar pauses at the threshold, looking back down the hall and then into the room.
Carrie enters last, carrying the stamped confirmation nobody else is looking at anymore.

title: I Brought Us Back
summary: Gunnar claims the return as his achievement while the issue lands on household continuity, not transit mastery for its own sake.

panelPlan.action: The household resumes around them: food on the table, bedding, key back on its hook, the stamped DTI paper set aside near Carrie's folder.
Bjorn takes off his coat.
Gunnar sets the MetroCards beside the household map, then looks at Bjorn.
Gunnar allows himself the distinction.
Carrie hears it while Astrid begins serving food.
